variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A computer-use agent is an AI system that observes a graphical interface, proposes mouse or keyboard actions, and uses the resulting interface state to continue a task. It can work in a browser, a desktop application, or a virtual machine even when the software has no purpose-built API.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Observation is evidence with blind spots”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Screenshot pixels
pairs.detail: Reveal canvas content, spatial relationships, overlays, and rendered state.
pairs.explanation: Reveal canvas content, spatial relationships, overlays, and rendered state. They are broad but expensive, hard to inspect precisely, and vulnerable to visually embedded instructions.

pairs.label: Accessibility semantics
pairs.detail: Expose roles, names, values, and control state when an application publishes them.
pairs.explanation: Expose roles, names, values, and control state when an application publishes them. Semantic targets are usually clearer than raw coordinates.

pairs.label: DOM or app state
pairs.detail: Provide attributes, URLs, network state, and stable application contracts.
pairs.explanation: Provide attributes, URLs, network state, and stable application contracts. They may omit pixels, canvas content, or native desktop elements.

pairs.label: Authoritative API
pairs.detail: Confirms durable effects such as a sent message, saved record, or completed payment.
pairs.explanation: Confirms durable effects such as a sent message, saved record, or completed payment. Prefer it over visual inference when it is available and authorized.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Computer use matters because graphical interfaces are stateful and only partly observable.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Screenshot pixels: Reveal canvas content, spatial relationships, overlays, and rendered state. Accessibility semantics: Expose roles, names, values, and control state when an application publishes them. DOM or app state: Provide attributes, URLs, network state, and stable application contracts. Authoritative API: Confirms durable effects such as a sent message, saved record, or completed payment.

variants.title: Give each part its job

It can work in a browser, a desktop application, or a virtual machine even when the software has no purpose-built API.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Separate the agent loop into owned boundaries”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Capture the environment
pairs.detail: Collect a screenshot and available semantics with a monotonic observation ID, timestamp, window identity, URL, account, and redaction policy.
pairs.explanation: Collect a screenshot and available semantics with a monotonic observation ID, timestamp, window identity, URL, account, and redaction policy.

pairs.label: Select one bounded action
pairs.detail: Identify the target, supporting evidence, expected postcondition, and what would make the proposal invalid before execution.
pairs.explanation: Identify the target, supporting evidence, expected postcondition, and what would make the proposal invalid before execution.

pairs.label: Evaluate authority
pairs.detail: Apply allowlists, identity, origin, data sensitivity, action risk, budgets, and current user approval outside the model.
pairs.explanation: Apply allowlists, identity, origin, data sensitivity, action risk, budgets, and current user approval outside the model.

pairs.label: Execute in isolation
pairs.detail: Use a browser, container, or VM with minimal privileges, restricted network access, scoped credentials, and controlled file exchange.
pairs.explanation: Use a browser, container, or VM with minimal privileges, restricted network access, scoped credentials, and controlled file exchange.

pairs.label: Check the postcondition
pairs.detail: Re-observe the interface and query authoritative state for consequential writes.
pairs.explanation: Re-observe the interface and query authoritative state for consequential writes. Record completed, rejected, failed, or ambiguous.

pairs.label: Continue or recover
pairs.explanation: Advance only from verified evidence. Otherwise re-plan, reconcile, ask the user, compensate, or stop according to the failure boundary.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A computer-use agent is an AI system that observes a graphical interface, proposes mouse or keyboard actions, and uses the resulting interface state to continue a task. It can work in a browser, a desktop application, or a virtual machine even when the software has no purpose-built API.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Permission follows the external effect”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Observe
pairs.detail: Reading a visible label or checking local state may proceed when the environment, account, and data policy allow it.
pairs.explanation: Reading a visible label or checking local state may proceed when the environment, account, and data policy allow it.

pairs.label: Prepare
pairs.detail: Filling a draft or assembling an upload can continue only when sensitive data has not yet been transmitted and the work remains reviewable.
pairs.explanation: Filling a draft or assembling an upload can continue only when sensitive data has not yet been transmitted and the work remains reviewable.

pairs.label: Transmit or commit
pairs.detail: Sending, posting, purchasing, sharing, uploading sensitive data, or changing access requires direct and current authorization for the exact effect.
pairs.explanation: Sending, posting, purchasing, sharing, uploading sensitive data, or changing access requires direct and current authorization for the exact effect.

pairs.label: Override a barrier
pairs.detail: Password changes, security warnings, CAPTCHA, or attempts to bypass a browser or website safeguard should be handed to the user or denied.
pairs.explanation: Password changes, security warnings, CAPTCHA, or attempts to bypass a browser or website safeguard should be handed to the user or denied.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Computer use matters because graphical interfaces are stateful and only partly observable.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Observe: Reading a visible label or checking local state may proceed when the environment, account, and data policy allow it. Prepare: Filling a draft or assembling an upload can continue only when sensitive data has not yet been transmitted and the work remains reviewable. Transmit or commit: Sending, posting, purchasing, sharing, uploading sensitive data, or changing access requires direct and current authorization for the exact effect. Override a barrier: Password changes, security warnings, CAPTCHA, or attempts to bypass a browser or website safeguard should be handed to the user or denied.

variants.prompt: Which statement is the core safety invariant for a computer-use agent?
options: A screenshot authorizes any action visible on the page.
An observation supports a proposal; trusted code authorizes the action and verifies the result.
A model-generated plan proves that its final action succeeded.
The browser's sandbox removes the need for action policy.
variants.explanation: Pixels and semantic state are evidence. Permission and proof of success come from trusted policy, direct user intent, and fresh or authoritative observations.
optionFeedback: Pixels and semantic state are evidence. Permission and proof of success come from trusted policy, direct user intent, and fresh or authoritative observations.

variants.hint: Think about the key idea first: In plain language: the model suggests how to use the screen, while your application captures observations, decides what is allowed, performs each action, and checks what actually happened.

Completed, because the click happened.

Rejected, then ask the model to guess.

Queue a three-click macro so the overlay has no time to change.
